title: Module 4 · IV to PO Conversions
intro: When to switch, the 1:1 drugs, the drugs that need a dose change, when not to switch, chelation, feeding tubes, linezolid interactions and how to run the daily IV to PO round.

cases.title: Is this patient ready for oral?
cases.stem: Day 3 of IV levofloxacin for community acquired pneumonia. Afebrile 36 hours, heart rate 84, BP 128/76, eating breakfast, WBC down from 16 to 9.

steps.q: Which findings support switching to oral?

options.t: Working gut: eating and taking other oral meds
A well absorbed oral option exists

options.why: Most criteria use 24 to 48 hours afebrile.

steps.q: What is the oral levofloxacin dose if she is on 750 mg IV daily?

options.why: 500 mg is an older levofloxacin dose; IV and PO are equivalent at 750 mg.
No adjustment for oral absorption needed.

steps.q: Why switch at all?

options.t: Fewer line infections, earlier discharge, lower cost
Oral antibiotics penetrate the lungs better

options.why: Renal adjustment applies by either route.

options.t: IV levofloxacin cannot be given beyond 3 days

cases.pearl: **Gut works, patient improving, good oral drug: switch.**

sources.t: Cyriac JM, James E. Switch over from intravenous to oral therapy: a concise overview. J Pharmacol Pharmacother 2014;5:83-87

cases.title: The 1:1 drugs
cases.stem: You are learning the drugs that convert at the same dose because oral absorption is excellent.

steps.q: Which convert 1:1 IV to PO?

options.why: About 70% absorbed: 400 mg IV = 500 to 750 mg PO.

steps.q: Which non antibiotics also convert about 1:1?

cases.pearl: **1:1 club: levo, moxi, linezolid, metronidazole, fluconazole, levetiracetam, APAP, pantoprazole.**

sources.t: Cyriac JM, James E. Switch over from intravenous to oral therapy: a concise overview. J Pharmacol Pharmacother 2014;5:83-87

cases.title: The drugs that do NOT convert 1:1
cases.stem: A team asks for help converting several drugs before discharge.

steps.q: Furosemide 40 mg IV twice daily. Roughly what oral dose gives similar effect?
Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV every 12 hours. Oral equivalent?

options.why: 1:1 is the levofloxacin rule, not ciprofloxacin.

steps.q: Metoprolol tartrate 5 mg IV every 6 hours. Oral equivalent?

options.t: About 12.5 to 25 mg PO every 6 hours
options.why: Roughly 1:2.5; titrate to heart rate and BP.
Lower daily total and a different product.

steps.q: Levothyroxine: how does IV compare with oral?

options.t: IV is lower: about 50 to 75% of oral
IV equals oral, microgram for microgram
IV is about double the oral dose
IV is about 25% of the oral dose

cases.pearl: **Not 1:1: furosemide (x2 oral), cipro (higher oral), metoprolol (about x2.5 oral), levothyroxine (IV lower).**

cases.title: When NOT to switch
cases.stem: A patient with MRSA bacteremia has been afebrile for 24 hours. The team asks about oral linezolid on day 3.

steps.q: Which situations usually stay IV, at least early?

options.why: Oral step down only in selected patients after clearance, with ID.
POET: partial oral therapy after at least 10 days IV in selected stable patients.

options.t: Community acquired pneumonia improving on day 3
options.why: Also a classic case for switching.

steps.q: Which patient factors block an oral switch?

options.t: Vomiting, ileus, severe diarrhea or malabsorption

options.why: Age alone does not block a switch.
Adjust the dose; route can still be oral.

cases.pearl: **Stay IV: S. aureus bacteremia early, meningitis, endocarditis (team decision), a gut that does not work.**

sources.t: Iversen K, et al. Partial oral versus intravenous antibiotic treatment of endocarditis (POET). N Engl J Med 2019;380:415-424

cases.title: Chelation: the switch that fails
cases.stem: Switched from IV to oral ciprofloxacin. The home med list includes calcium carbonate, a multivitamin with iron and zinc, and magnesium oxide.

steps.q: What is the problem?

options.t: Ca, Mg, Al, Fe and Zn bind ciprofloxacin

options.why: The problem is binding in the gut, not clearance.

steps.q: What do you recommend?

options.t: Cipro 2 h before or 6 h after the minerals
options.why: Per label; or hold supplements during the course.

options.t: Cipro 6 h before or 2 h after the minerals

steps.q: Which other oral antibiotics have the same chelation problem?

cases.pearl: **Quinolones and tetracyclines + Ca, Mg, Al, Fe, Zn = no absorption. Space them.**

sources.t: DailyMed prescribing information for each drug named (Clinical Pharmacology and Drug Interactions sections)

cases.title: Feeding tube conversions
cases.setting: ICU · new NG tube with continuous feeds
cases.stem: A patient on continuous tube feeds needs phenytoin and levothyroxine switched from IV to the tube.

steps.q: What is the issue with phenytoin suspension and tube feeds?

options.t: Feeds bind it; hold feeds 1 to 2 h around doses
Feeds have no effect on phenytoin

steps.q: Phenytoin capsules versus suspension: why can the dose change?

options.t: Both forms are phenytoin acid at 100%
Only IV phenytoin is the sodium salt

steps.q: Which products should NOT be crushed for the tube?

options.t: Extended release and enteric coated tablets
options.why: Check the ISMP Do Not Crush list.

options.t: Plain immediate release metoprolol tartrate tablets
options.why: Can be crushed; the succinate ER cannot.

cases.pearl: **Tube feeds: phenytoin and feeds do not mix, salt forms differ, never crush ER or EC.**

cases.title: Linezolid switch, interaction check
cases.stem: Switching IV linezolid 600 mg every 12 hours to oral. Home meds include sertraline.

steps.q: What dose orally?
What interaction do you check?
What lab do you watch on longer courses?

options.t: Platelets and counts after about 2 weeks

cases.pearl: **Linezolid 1:1, but check for SSRIs and watch platelets.**

cases.title: Doing the IV to PO round
cases.stem: You run the daily IV to PO report for your units.

steps.q: How do you make the switch happen?

options.t: Use the automatic conversion protocol when eligible
Recommend to the prescriber with criteria and dose
Switch everything on day 3 without checking
Wait for the prescriber to ask
options.why: Proactive switching is the pharmacist's value.

cases.call: "Dr. ___, your patient in 412 is afebrile 48 hours, eating, and on IV metronidazole 500 mg every 8 hours. Oral metronidazole is nearly 100% absorbed. May I change it to 500 mg PO every 8 hours?"
cases.pearl: **Run the report daily. Protocol where allowed, a clear recommendation everywhere else.**
